questions.question: Swati sold a bag to Ankita at a gain of 15%. Aashi bought this bag from Ankita for Rs. 24,840. Ankita earned a profit of 20%. At what price would Swati have bought the bag?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Swati at a gain of 15% sold a bag to Ankita 

Aashi bought the bag at Rs24,840 

Ankita earned a profit o f 20%

**FORMULA USED:**

S.P. = ( 100 + P%)/100 × C.P. 

Where S.P. = Selling Price and C.P. = Cost price 

**CALCULATION:**

Here, Aashi bought the bag from Ankita at Rs24840 

So, Selling Price of Ankita = Rs24840

Profit% of Ankita = 20%

Now, as we know 

S.P. = ( 100 + P%) /100 × C.P.

⇒ 24840 = 120/100 × C.P. 

Cost Price of Ankita = Rs20700

As, Swati sold a bag to Ankita 

So, Cost price of Ankita = Selling Price of Swati = Rs20700

Profit% of Swati = 15%

Again,

⇒ 20700 = 115/100 × C.P. 

 C.P. = Rs18,000

**Hence, Cost Price of Swati is Rs18,000**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Swati sold a bag to Ankita at a gain of 15%, Swati : Ankita = 20 : 23

Again Ankita sold it to Ashi at a gain of 20% , Ankita : Ashi = 5 : 6

So, Swati : Ankita : Ashi = 100 : 115 : 138

Now, 138 unit → 24840,

Then 100 unit → 24840/138 × 100 = 18000

questions.question: Geeta runs 5/2 times as fast as Babita. In a race, if Geeta gives a lead of 40 m to Babita, find the distance from the starting point where both of them will meet (correct up to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds (Geeta : Babita) = 5 : 2

Since time is constant, Distance ratio = Speed ratio = 5 : 2

Difference in distance (Lead) = 5 − 2 = 3 units

3 units → 40 m

Distance from start (Geeta's total distance) = 5 units = (40 ÷ 3) × 5 = 200 ÷ 3 ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Geeta = 5/2 × Speed of Babita

Lead given to Babita = 40 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e111aa4b516ba1a065e38b23005ef18c6e237fc517c85e3d2df0f10667dac5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of Babita be 2x and the speed of Geeta be 5x.

⇒ Let the meeting point be at a distance D from the starting point.

⇒ Since they meet at the same time:

⇒ Time taken by Geeta = Time taken by Babita

⇒ D ÷ 5x = (D − 40) ÷ 2x

⇒ D ÷ 5 = (D − 40) ÷ 2

⇒ 2D = 5 × (D − 40)

⇒ 2D = 5D − 200

⇒ 3D = 200

⇒ D = 200 ÷ 3 = 66.666...

⇒ D ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Races

When two people move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂.

Distance-Speed Relationship

If time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂). If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Concept of Lead

A "lead of x meters" means the slower runner starts x meters ahead of the faster runner. To meet, the faster runner must cover this extra distance using their relative speed.</p

questions.question: In a showroom the price of a washing machine is ₹65,000. The customer gets cash discount of ₹2,000, and gets a scratch card promising percentage discount of 10% to 15%. Determine the difference between the least and the maximum selling prices of the washing machine.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Price of a washing price is Rs65,000 

Cash discount = Rs2,000 

Percentage discount of 10% to 15% 

**FORMULA USED:**

S.P. = C.P. × ( 100 - d%)/100 

Where, S.P. = Selling price , C.P. = Cost price and d = discount%

**CALCULATION:**

Here, the price of a washing machine is Rs65,000 and cash discount is Rs2,000 

Price of washing machine after cash discount = ( 65,000 - 2000 ) = Rs63,000 

Now, percentage discount of 10% to 15% is given 

Maximum selling price of washing machine = 63,000 × 90/100 = 56,700 

Least selling price of washing machine = 63,000 × 85 /100 = 53,550 

Difference = 56,700 - 53,550 = Rs3,150 

**Hence, difference between maximum and least selling price is Rs3,150 .**

questions.question: The simplified form of (7x + 4y)² + (7x − 4y)² is:
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

(7x + 4y)² + ( 7x - 4y)² 

**FORMULA USED:**

( a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab 

( a - b)² = a²+ b² - 2ab 

**CALCULATION:**

Here,

( 7x + 4y)² = 49x² + 16y² + 2 × 7x × 4y = 49x² + 16y² + 56xy 

(7x - 4y)² = 49x² + 16y² - 2 × 7x × 4y = 49x² +16y² - 56xy 

⇒ (7x + 4y)² + ( 7x - 4y)² = 49x² + 16y² + 56xy + 49x² + 16y² -56xy = 98x² + 32y²

**Hence, the required value is 98x² + 32y² .**

questions.question: A man bought two bicycles for ₹3,000 each. If he sells one bicycle at a profit of 10%, then for how much percentage profit should he sell the other bicycle so that he makes a profit of 20% on the whole?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A man bought two bicycles for Rs3,000 

If he sells one bicycle at a profit of 10% 

Profit of 20% on the whole 

**FORMULA USED:**

Profit% = Profit/C.P. × 100 

Profit = S.P. - C.P. 

Where, S.P. = Selling price and C.P. = Cost price 

**CALCULATION:**

Here, C.P. of bicycles = Rs3,000 each 

One bicycle is sold at a profit of 10% 

S.P. of the bicycle = 3,000 × 110/100 = Rs3,300 

Also, profit of 20% on the whole and total C.P. = Rs6,000 

Total S.P. = 6,000 × 120/100 = Rs7,200 

S.P. of other bicycle = ( 7200 - 3300) = 3,900 and C.P. of other bicycle = 3,000

Profit =(3,900 - 3,000) = 9,00 

Percentage profit = 900/3000 × 100 = 30

**Hence, the required profit percentage is 30 percent.**

Now, eq(5) + eq(6)

⇒ 44/x = 22 ⇔ x = 2 

Now, put the value of x = 2 in the eq(1), we get

questions.question:
As shown in the given figure, inside the large semicircle, three semicircles (with equal radii) are drawn so that their diameters all sit on the large semicircle's diameter. What is the ratio between the red and blue areas?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3df805746ec1c06b3f432f53781daf74182e80a60bd29ea15dd54e57c4d3db78.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three smaller semicircles with equal radii sit in a bigger semicircle

**Formula used:**

Area of semicircle = (πr²)/(2)

Where, r = radius of the semicircle

**Calculation:**

Let the radius of the smaller semicircle be 'r'

According to the question,

So the radius of the bigger semicircle with respect to the smaller circle will be '3r'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2277b67b07ef322786288cba5fc82f3c8267c921602604521cc3d67ec3e97dc.png] 

Area of the small semicircle = (πr²)/(2)

Area of the large semicircle = (π(3r)²)/(2) = (9π r²)/(2)

Red area = 3 × Area of the small semicircle

Red area = (3πr²)/(2)

Blue area = Area of the large semicircle - Red area

= (9π r²)/(2) - (3πr²)/(2) = (6πr²)/(2)

Blue area = 3πr²

(Red area)/(Blue area) = (frac{3πr²)/(2)}{3πr²} = (1)/(2)

Red area : Blue area = 1 : 2

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2)**.

questions.question: A car covered the first 100 km at a speed of 50 km/h. It covered next 140 km at a speed of 70 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A car covered the first 100 km at a speed of 50 km/h 

Next 140 km at speed of 70km/h 

**FORMULA USED:**

Average Speed = Total distance travelled/Total time taken

**CALCULATION:**

Here,

Car covered first 100km at a speed of 50km/h 

Time taken = 100/50 = 2 h

Now,

Next 140 km at speed of 70km/h 

Time taken = 140/70 = 2 

Total distance = ( 100 + 140 ) = 240km 

Total time taken = 4 h 

Average speed = 240 /4 = 60km/h 

**Hence, its average speed is 60km/h .**

questions.question: What is the length of the longest pole that can fit itself in a hall 60 feet long, 30 feet broad and 20 feet high?
questions.solution:

A hall is 60 feet long 30 feet broad and 20 feet high 

**FORMULA USED:**

Length of diagonal of a cuboid = sqrt{l² +b² + h²}

Where, l= length , b= breadth ,h = height 

**CALCULATION:**

Here, hall has length = 60 feet , breadth = 30 feet and height = 20 feet 

As, the length of the longest rod that can be placed in a room is it's diagonal 

Now, the length of diagonal of a cuboid = sqrt{l² + b² + h²} 

So, length of the longest rod = sqrt{60² + 30² + 20²} = sqrt{4900} = 70 feet 

**Hence, length of the longest rod is 70 feet .**

questions.question:
What are the values of R and M, respectively, if the given number is perfectly divisible by 16 and 11 ?

34R05030M6
questions.solution:
**Given**:

34R05030M6

16 and 11

**Concept used:**

A number is divisible by 11, if the difference of the sum of odd and even places is divisible by 11.

**Solution:**

To be divisible by 11,

[(3 + R + 5 + 3 + M) - (4 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 6)] % 11 = 0

11 + R + M - 10 % 11 = 0

1 + R + M must be a multiple of 11

R + M = 10

questions.question: The LCM and HCF of two numbers are 126 and 9, respectively. If one of the numbers is 18, then what is the other number?

questions.question: Two stations are 120 km apart on a straight line. A train starts from station A at 8 a.m. and moves towards station B at 20 km/h, and another train starts from station B at 9 a.m. and travels towards station A at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

D = 120 km

A = 8 am = 20 km/h

B = 9 am = 30 km/h

**Concept used:**

Relative speed opposite direction = Sum of speeds

Speed = Distance/Time 

**Solution:**

Relative speed = 20 = 30 = 50 km/h

Distance covered by 1st Train in 1 hour = 20 km

Distance left = 120 - 20 = 100 km

Total time = 100/50 = 2 hours

They will meet at 8 am = 1 + 2 = 11 am

**Hence, the correct option is 3.**

questions.question: The least common multiple of 48 and 64 is _____ times the highest common factor of 12 and 18.
questions.solution:

It is the product of the greatest power of each prime factor, involved in the numbers.

questions.question: If cos 48° = (m)/(n), then sec 48° - cot 42° is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

cos 48° = (m)/(n) 

**Formula used:**

cos theta = (b)/(h)

sec theta = (h)/(b)

tan theta = (p)/(b)

cot (90° - theta) = tan theta

h² = p² + b²

Where, h = hypotenuse, p = perpendicular, b = base 

**Calculation:**

Here, we have 

cos 48° = (b)/(h) = (m)/(n) 

h² = p² + b²

⇒ n² = p² + m²

⇒ p = sqrt{n² - m²} 

As, we know that 

sec 48° = (h)/(b) =(n)/(m )

cot 42° = cot (90° - 48°) = tan 48° ...............[As cot (90° - theta) = tan theta] 

tan 48° = (p)/(b) = frac{sqrt{ n² - m²}}{m}

So, sec 48° - cot 42° = sec 48° - tan 48°

⇒ (n)/(m) - frac{sqrt{n² - m²}}{m} = n - sqrt{ n² - m²}over m 

**Hence, the required value is n - sqrt{n² - m²}over m**.

questions.question: At a construction site, Raju can paint a wall in 36 hours, while Angad can do the same work in 18 hours. Sumit can paint the same wall in 24 hours. In how much time can they paint the wall if they all work together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 36, 18, and 24 = 72 units.

Combined efficiency = (72 ÷ 36) + (72 ÷ 18) + (72 ÷ 24).

Combined efficiency = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 units/hour.

Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Raju = 36 hours

Time taken by Angad = 18 hours

Time taken by Sumit = 24 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency = Raju's efficiency + Angad's efficiency + Sumit's efficiency

⇒ Total efficiency = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 units/hour

⇒ Time taken by all three working together = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes do positive work (filling), while outlet pipes do negative work (emptying). Net efficiency determines the total time to fill or empty the tank.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each individual. If multiple people work together for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When workers operate on alternate days, you must calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible before calculating the remaining days individually.

If 16% = 4480, then 100% (Total Votes) = (4480 ÷ 16) × 100 = 28000.
